_about: One sentence per kind NAME (the noun a seller writes in the title and a buyer types), the cup-set library archetype(s) of kind-layer spec v2 Part I.4 it is built from, and whether the name is in that library. III.4 asserts 'kind names not in the library: 0' — every in_library:false row is an open item, named rather than hidden. Written by the parent 13 Sep 2026 from the spec and the classifier headers; a definition is a statement of intent, the classifier rules and the witness rows on each kind page are the evidence.

access-point.note: the library name is `ap`; meraki spells it `access-point` — a rule-3 naming disagreement

accessory.definition: A part the axis could not place more precisely (unresolved) — asked only what it fits.

adapter.definition: A form-factor converter that lets one pluggable fit another cage (QSA, CVR adapters).

amplifier.definition: An optical amplifier (EDFA) that boosts a DWDM or HFC optical signal.

analytics.definition: A flow/log analytics appliance (Secure Network Analytics, Stealthwatch collectors).

antenna.definition: An external antenna for Wi-Fi or cellular radios.

appliance.definition: A rack or desktop appliance that is not a router, switch or firewall (management, WAAS, WLC-appliance, mobile-core boxes).

ata.definition: An analog telephone adapter connecting analog phones to IP telephony.

backhaul.definition: A point-to-point or mesh wireless backhaul radio.
backhaul.note: the library has no BACKHAUL archetype; asked a subset of AP

breakout-cable.definition: A cable with one high-speed end breaking out into several lower-speed ends.

bundle.definition: A single orderable number that contains several parts (a pack or a card complement); asked its contents.
bundle.note: bundle is a registered-derivation kind (bundle_contents), not a library archetype

cable.definition: A length of data cable (DAC, AOC, fibre patch, console, stacking is separate).

camera.definition: A video camera for conferencing or surveillance.

cellular.definition: A cellular (LTE/5G) modem module for a router.

chassis.definition: An empty modular chassis that takes supervisors, line cards and power supplies.

compute.definition: A compute sled or server blade inside a security platform.
compute.note: security's name; the library would call it `server`

controller.definition: A controller/shelf-controller card of an optical platform.
controller.note: optical-networking's name for a shelf controller

dcu.definition: A dispersion compensation unit for DWDM spans.

dect-base.definition: A DECT base station for cordless IP phones.

device.definition: A whole device filed in interfaces-modules (the axis could not name which).
device.note: a wrong-table signal: interfaces-modules holds cards, not devices

director.note: spec II.12 target kind; no library archetype of its own

display.definition: A display screen for a room system or desk.

drive.definition: A storage drive (HDD, SSD, NVMe) option.

expansion-module.definition: A key expansion module that clips onto a desk phone.

fabric.definition: A fabric module that interconnects line cards inside a chassis.

fabric-interconnect.definition: A UCS fabric interconnect switch that manages servers.

fan.definition: A fan tray or fan module.

fc-switch.definition: A fixed Fibre Channel storage switch (MDS 9100/9200/9300).

fex.definition: A fabric extender (Nexus 2000): a port box that forwards everything to its parent switch.
fex.note: spec II.1: ports, uplink_ports, power_max, psu_config, airflow, product_compatibility + ENV; NOT ETH-SWITCHING

flash.definition: A flash memory card or module for a router.
flash.note: routers' own name; the library folds flash cards into MEMORY

gateway.definition: A voice gateway (analog/digital trunks to IP) or a Meraki cellular gateway.

gpu.definition: A GPU accelerator card option for a server.

headset.definition: A headset for phones and soft clients.

interface.definition: A plug-in interface card (NIM, HWIC, EHWIC, SM, EPA) that adds ports to a router or switch.

io-module.definition: An I/O module of a blade chassis (UCS IOM / fabric extender module).
io-module.note: UCS name; no library archetype of its own

ips-module.definition: An IPS module inside a firewall or router.
ips-module.note: spec III.1 folds ips-module into `module`; not yet renamed

linecard.definition: A line card that takes a chassis slot and carries ports.

mechanical.definition: A mechanical part: rack kit, bezel, cover, bracket, blank.

microphone.definition: A table or ceiling microphone for room systems.

module.definition: A network, uplink, service or daughter module that goes into a fixed device or a card.
module.note: absorbs switches' daughter and stack-module (spec III.1, done in db24763)

nic.definition: A network interface card for a server.

non-product.definition: An orderable number that is not a product (tracking, rebate, placeholder) — belongs in class non_product.
non-product.note: a class, not a kind: every row is pending a class change

optic.definition: A pluggable or fixed optic filed in video or interfaces-modules.
optic.note: the library name is `pluggable` (transceiver); a wrong-table signal

os-license.definition: An operating-system licence (VMware, RHEL, Windows) sold with a server — belongs in class license.
os-license.note: a class, not a kind: pending a class change

passive.definition: A passive HFC/optical component (splitter, coupler, filter).

pdu.note: the PDU library is the PSU library minus airflow (nameMarker test)

phone.definition: An IP phone (desk, wireless, DECT or conference).

plug-in.definition: A plug-in card for an HFC headend chassis (Prisma II).

pluggable.definition: A pluggable optical transceiver (SFP, QSFP, CFP…).

pluggable-bidi.definition: A bidirectional pluggable filed in optical-networking.

pluggable-tunable.definition: A tunable DWDM pluggable filed in optical-networking.

power-cord.definition: A mains or DC power cord.

processor.definition: A route processor or forwarding processor card (RSP, RP, ESP).

radio.definition: An 802.11 radio module for a router or AP.

rf-amplifier.definition: An RF (coax) amplifier in an HFC plant.

roadm.definition: A reconfigurable optical add-drop multiplexer card.
roadm.note: the library folds ROADM into MUX

router.definition: A router (branch, SMB, edge, industrial IoT).

security-module.definition: A security/crypto module inside a device.
security-module.note: spec III.1 folds security-module into `module`; not yet renamed

sensor.definition: An environmental/wireless sensor (Meraki MT, Catalyst wireless sensor).

server.definition: A server (rack, blade, modular node, edge, storage).

software.definition: A software image or licence filed as hardware — belongs in class software/license.
software.note: III.4: software rows in any hardware kind = 0; pending class change

sp-core.definition: A service-provider core/edge routing system (ASR 9000, CRS, NCS 5500/540, 8000).

stack-cable.definition: A stacking cable between stackable switches.

storage-controller.definition: A RAID / storage controller card for a server.

supervisor.definition: A supervisor engine that runs a modular switch.

switch.definition: An Ethernet switch (SMB, access, core/aggregation, data center, industrial).

system.definition: An HFC headend platform chassis (Prisma II).

touch-panel.definition: A touch controller for room systems.

tpm.definition: A trusted platform module for a server.
tpm.note: UCS name-only kind; no library archetype

transceiver.definition: A transceiver filed under a collaboration category.
transceiver.note: a wrong-table signal: transceivers belong in category transceiver as `pluggable`

unknown.definition: A part the axis could not place (unresolved); asked nothing it may not have.
unknown.note: the one sanctioned unresolved name (spec III.1: other -> unknown)

video-codec.definition: A video conferencing codec (the box that encodes/decodes for a room).

video-device.definition: An integrated video room system or desk video device.

voice-module.definition: A voice interface module (VIC, PVDM) for a router or gateway.
voice-module.note: no library archetype of its own

switch.industrial: Industrial and ruggedised switches (IE 2000/3000/4000/5000/IE9300, CGS, ESS).

ap.mesh-extender: Mesh extenders that repeat another AP's signal.

router.branch: Branch routers (ISR, Catalyst 8200/8300/8500 edge in the branch).
router.edge: WAN edge / aggregation routers (ASR 1000, Catalyst 8500, 8000 edge).
router.industrial-iot: Industrial IoT routers and gateways (IR, CGR).
